newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner wins 320 mln NOK offshore deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner wins 320 mln NOK offshore deal.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Kvaerner ASA said on Tuesday it had won a contract with state-owned Statoil AS worth 320 million crowns.

A statement said Kvaerner subsidiary Kvaerner Oilfield Products would supply Statoil, formally known as Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, with subsea steel control cables for platforms in the North Sea and the Norwegian Sea.
Kvaerner said the order represented a boost for its leading position in the market for umbilicals.
The steel cables will be delivered to the Gullfaks, Rimfaks and Rimveig fields in the North Sea and to Smorbukk, Midgard and Smorbukk South in the Norwegian Sea.
The contract for has been awarded by Kongsverg Offshore AS, which is the main supplier of subsea oil and gas production equipment to Statoil.
The statement said the contract also contained options for future supplies to both Gullfaks and Midgard.
